Name: whisper_calm_nospeech_schm
Title: Silence-Conditional Decoder Head Masking for Whisper Non-Speech Hallucinations
Short Hypothesis: Masking Whisper's hallucinatory decoder heads {1,6,11} only when p_no_speech is high will preserve most of the hallucination reduction of always-masking while recovering most of the WER loss on speech -- a Pareto-dominant inference-time tradeoff requiring no training.
Related Work: Calm-Whisper (Wang et al., 2025) identifies hallucinatory decoder heads via head-wise masking and reduces hallucinations via selective head fine-tuning. Careless Whisper (Koenecke et al., 2024) documents hallucination harms in ASR. Whisper (Radford et al., 2022) includes no_speech_threshold heuristic. WhisperX (Bain et al., 2023) uses VAD preprocessing. No prior work proposes no-speech-triggered decoder head masking for hallucination mitigation.

notes: Whisper-large-v3 is only ~3GB VRAM -- trivially fits RTX 5080
Cannot use Gemini API (needs model internals for head masking)
Phase-1 go/no-go: refute if <30% of hallucinating clips have p_no_speech > 0.5
